intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Witness the breathtaking sunrise over the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex, one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs and towering spires that tell the story of the ancient Khmer Empire. A guided tour helps bring the history and symbolism of this UNESCO World Heritage Site to life.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Beachfront Snorkeling Adventure
experiences.description: Explore the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounding Koh Rong island, one of Cambodia's most stunning beach destinations. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, and relax on pristine white-sand beaches. Many tours include a boat trip around the island with stops at secluded coves.

experiences.name: Sihanoukville Beachfront Khmer Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef near the beachfront in Sihanoukville. Learn to prepare authentic Khmer dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and mango salad using fresh local ingredients sourced from nearby markets. Enjoy your creations with ocean views as a backdrop.

experiences.name: Kep Crab Market and Coastal Village Walk
experiences.description: Visit the famous Kep Crab Market, a beloved coastal institution where local fishermen bring in their daily catch. Sample freshly cooked Kampot pepper crab — a regional delicacy — and stroll through the charming seaside village of Kep, exploring its French colonial ruins and lush national park trails along the coast.

experiences.name: Otres Beach Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle along the calm, scenic waters of Otres Beach at sunset, one of Cambodia's most relaxed and beautiful coastal stretches. Kayak through mangrove channels and along the shoreline while watching the sky turn golden over the Gulf of Thailand. This peaceful activity offers a perfect blend of nature, history of the coastline, and cultural scenery.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Take a gentle orientation walk around the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate area to get your bearings and photograph the iconic stone faces. Pick up a 3-day Angkor Pass from the official ticket booth (budget ~$62 USD) to use over the next few days.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Siem Reap's Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chaa) area for a relaxed first evening. Browse street stalls, soak up the atmosphere, and enjoy a cheap street-food dinner. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or hotel on arrival — try a local noodle soup (kuy teav) from a roadside stall for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.dinner: Pub Street area: try Khmer Kitchen Restaurant for authentic local dishes like amok (fish curry) and lok lak (stir-fried beef) — budget ~$4–6 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport or a local money changer. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area cost ~$8–10 USD. Negotiate fares upfront.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Watch the temple reflect in the lotus ponds as the sky turns gold. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and upper terraces (~3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or cycle to the nearby Angkor Thom complex. Explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then visit the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Hire a local guide at the gate for ~$15 USD for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel to freshen up. Visit the Siem Reap Night Market for souvenir shopping and street food. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance if available at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a baguette (French colonial influence) from a street vendor near Angkor Wat — ~$1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style: buy fresh fruit, rice cakes, and coconut water from vendors outside Angkor Thom — ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Siem Reap Night Market food stalls: grilled skewers, fried rice, and fresh spring rolls — budget ~$3–5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Rent a bicycle near your hotel for ~$2–3 USD/day to explore Angkor independently — eco-friendly and budget-savvy. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) to enter temple complexes. Carry water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-swallowed Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) — massive silk-cotton trees grow through the ancient stone walls in a hauntingly beautiful way. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist monastery temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Srah Srang, the Royal Bathing Pool, for a peaceful lakeside moment. Then head to Pre Rup, a 10th-century temple mountain, for panoramic views over the jungle — perfect for late-afternoon photography as the light turns warm and golden.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local Angkor Night Market. Attend a free cultural show or browse handmade Cambodian crafts. Try a traditional Khmer massage for ~$6–8 USD/hour — a budget-friendly treat after a day of walking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery near the park — $1–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant near Ta Prohm: rice with grilled chicken and vegetables — ~$2.50–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Try Mahob Restaurant or a similar local Khmer eatery in Siem Reap town: fish amok, green mango salad, and jasmine rice — ~$5–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm can be crowded midday — go early morning. Your 3-day Angkor Pass covers all temples visited today. Stay hydrated; November can still be warm (~28–32°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Banteay Srei temple (~38 km from Siem Reap), famous for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the jewel of Khmer art. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day (~$15–20 USD round trip). En route, stop at the Landmine Museum (donation-based entry) to learn about Cambodia's tragic recent history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Cambodian Cultural Village (entry ~$9 USD) on the way back to Siem Reap for a condensed overview of Cambodia's ethnic groups, traditional architecture, and cultural performances — great for history and culture lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Siem Reap River walkway. Visit the Old Market (Psar Chaa) for last-minute browsing. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with free entry (just buy one drink).

meals.breakfast: Local market breakfast: num banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce) — a beloved Cambodian morning staple, ~$1–1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a roadside stall near Banteay Srei — fresh coconut and rice dishes ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Siem Reap town: Bugs Cafe (adventurous — try insects!) or a safe classic like Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training restaurant) — ~$5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Today uses your final day on the 3-day Angkor Pass if you purchased a consecutive pass. Banteay Srei is covered under the Angkor Pass. Tuk-tuk drivers often double as informal guides — negotiate a full-day rate.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk is scenic and less touristy than Chong Kneas). Boat tours cost ~$10–15 USD and offer a fascinating glimpse into life on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop in Siem Reap (free entry) — watch skilled Cambodian craftspeople create silk textiles, lacquerware, and stone carvings using traditional techniques. A wonderful cultural and ethical shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Siem Reap by overnight bus or evening minivan toward Phnom Penh (~6–7 hours, ~$8–12 USD with companies like Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Book in advance for the best seats.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or guesthouse breakfast — $1–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Floating village area: fresh fish soup or grilled fish from local vendors — ~$3–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Grab a packed dinner or eat before boarding the bus: Siem Reap market banh mi sandwich or rice box — ~$2–3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Phnom Penh accommodation in advance. Giant Ibis is the most reputable budget bus company in Cambodia with reclining seats and onboard WiFi. Overnight buses save on one night's accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Phnom Penh early morning. Check into a budget guesthouse (~$8–15 USD/night in BKK1 or Riverside area). After freshening up, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10 USD) — a stunning complex of Khmer architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and the famous floor of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Museum of Cambodia (entry ~$5 USD) — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts spanning 1,000 years of history. Then stroll along the Tonlé Sap Riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Street 278 and Street 240 areas for cafes and local bars. Visit the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) before it closes for handicrafts and souvenirs at lower prices than Siem Reap.

meals.breakfast: Bus station or nearby cafe: coffee and a croissant or rice porridge (babor) — ~$1.50–2.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the Royal Palace: lok lak with rice and iced tea — ~$3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Riverside area: Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise, traditional Khmer food in a beautiful villa) — ~$7–10 USD, worth the slight splurge.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is easily navigable by tuk-tuk (~$2–4 per ride) or PassApp (Cambodia's Grab equivalent). The city is more spread out than Siem Reap. Stay aware of your belongings in busy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison, entry ~$8 USD) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison that held 17,000 prisoners. A deeply sobering and essential historical experience to understand Cambodia's recent past. Audio guides are available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from city center, entry ~$6 USD including audio guide). The memorial stupa containing thousands of skulls is a powerful and haunting tribute to the victims of the Khmer Rouge genocide (1975–1979).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city. Visit the lively Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco dome building — for browsing and street food. Walk along the riverside at dusk and watch locals doing evening aerobics in Riverside Park.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local coffee shop: iced Cambodian coffee (strong and sweet) with bread and egg — ~$2 USD.
meals.lunch: Near Tuol Sleng: Friends the Restaurant (social enterprise) — excellent Khmer tapas and fresh juices — ~$5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Central Market area: street food stalls — grilled corn, beef skewers, fried noodles — ~$2–4 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — take your time and be respectful. The audio guide at Choeung Ek is narrated by survivors and is highly recommended. Allow a full morning/afternoon for both sites.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or minivan from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, ~$7–10 USD) — Cambodia's main beach gateway. Check into a budget guesthouse on Otres Beach (~$10–15 USD/night), which is quieter and more relaxed than Serendipity Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on Otres Beach — a long, relatively uncrowded stretch of golden sand with calm turquoise waters. Swim, sunbathe, or rent a kayak (~$5 USD/hour) to explore the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Enjoy a beach bonfire if your guesthouse organizes one. Explore the laid-back Otres Village strip of beach bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Grab food on the bus or at the Phnom Penh bus station before departure — rice or sandwiches ~$1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Beachside shack near Otres: fresh seafood (grilled squid, prawn) with rice — ~$4–6 USD.
meals.dinner: Otres Beach bar-restaurant: BBQ seafood platter, fresh fruit shake, and Angkor beer — ~$6–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Sihanoukville's main beach area (Victory Beach, Serendipity) has become heavily developed. Otres Beach (Otres 1 and 2) remains the best budget-friendly and scenic option. Book accommodation in advance during November (end of rainy season, beginning of peak season).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day-trip boat to Koh Rong Sanloem island (~45 min ferry, ~$20–25 USD return) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful islands with pristine white-sand beaches, crystal-clear water, and coral reefs. Spend the morning snorkeling off Lazy Beach or M'Pai Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot — hike through jungle trails to secluded beaches. Visit the bioluminescent plankton bay (best seen at night, but the bay is beautiful by day too). Swim and relax on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sihanoukville on the late afternoon ferry. Back at Otres Beach, enjoy a final relaxed beach dinner. If you stayed overnight on the island (optional upgrade), enjoy the famous bioluminescent plankton in the bay after dark — a magical natural phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast on Otres Beach before catching the ferry — $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: On Koh Rong Sanloem: beachside restaurant — fresh fish curry, coconut rice, and green mango salad — ~$5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Otres Beach: grilled barracuda or red snapper with vegetables and rice at a local beach shack — ~$5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets to Koh Rong Sanloem can be booked at the Sihanoukville pier or through your guesthouse. Last ferry back is usually around 5:00–5:30 PM — confirm times locally. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Otres Beach — take a slow sunrise walk along the shore, swim one last time, and sip a fresh coconut. Pack up and check out. Pick up any last souvenirs from the beach market stalls (silk scarves, handmade jewelry, Cambodian pepper).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Phnom Penh by bus (~4 hours) or arrange an onward connection depending on your departure flight. If time allows before your flight, visit the Independence Monument and stroll through the French Quarter of Phnom Penh for a final taste of the city's colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, floating villages, tragic history, and stunning beaches. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring one of Southeast Asia's most fascinating and resilient countries.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast on the beach: fresh fruit platter, banana pancake, and iced coffee — ~$2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Bus stop or Phnom Penh: banh mi sandwich or noodle soup — ~$1.50–2.50 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport or departure meal — budget ~$5–10 USD depending on location.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated 10-day budget breakdown: Accommodation ~$80–130 USD, Food ~$80–120 USD, Transport ~$60–80 USD, Entrance fees ~$100–120 USD, Activities ~$50–70 USD. Grand total: approximately $370–520 USD for 10 days — very achievable on a budget. Always carry small USD bills and some Riel for local markets.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel near Angkor Archaeological Park and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride to the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate for an introductory look at the ancient city walls and iconic stone face towers. Stroll along the causeway lined with gods and demons — a perfect gentle introduction to Angkor's scale and grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in Siem Reap for a vibrant first evening. Explore the night market stalls selling local crafts and silks, then settle in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant or a nearby café such as Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise serving authentic Khmer dishes at mid-range prices.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant near Pub Street — excellent Khmer cuisine including amok fish curry and lok lak beef. Budget around $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency to Cambodian Riel (KHR) or use USD at the airport. Arrange a multi-day Angkor Pass at the hotel or at the official Angkor ticket office — a 3-day pass ($62) is ideal. Keep the afternoon light due to travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:00 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Watch the temple's five towers reflect in the lotus ponds as the sun rises. Spend the early morning hours exploring Angkor Wat's outer galleries, bas-relief carvings depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the inner sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning break, visit the Bayon Temple inside Angkor Thom — famous for its 216 serene stone faces. Then walk to Baphuon Temple and the Elephant Terrace. End with a visit to Ta Prohm, the jungle temple famously wrapped in massive tree roots (the 'Tomb Raider' temple).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a traditional Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized art form. Several restaurants host nightly shows with dinner included.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before sunrise departure — grab a banana and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the temples or eat at one of the local food stalls inside the Angkor complex. Try bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) for around $2–4.
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara dance show at Angkor Village Resort or Koulen Restaurant — set menu approximately $15–20 per person including the performance.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and comfortable walking shoes. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a refillable water bottle. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temples. Start the sunrise visit by 5:15 AM for the best reflection views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but spectacular Banteay Srei temple, located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' it features extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. Combine with a visit to the nearby Banteay Samré temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (Cambodian Landmine Museum) on the way back — a sobering and important cultural stop that documents Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing humanitarian effort to clear them. Then visit Preah Khan temple, a sprawling jungle monastery with long atmospheric corridors.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel pool or spa, then head out for a quieter evening exploring the artisan village of Artisans Angkor workshop near the hotel area.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel — most boutique hotels in Angkor area include breakfast. Enjoy Khmer porridge (bobor) or eggs with baguette.
meals.lunch: Stop at a local village restaurant near Banteay Srei for a simple Khmer lunch — try samlor machu (sour soup) for around $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Restaurant in Siem Reap — a beloved local favorite specializing in traditional Khmer recipes. Expect $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the full day to reach Banteay Srei — negotiate a full-day rate of approximately $20–25. The Landmine Museum charges a small entrance fee ($3–5) that goes directly to the charitable organization.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — one of the largest freshwater lakes in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the famous floating villages of Kampong Phluk or Chong Kneas, where entire communities live on stilted houses or floating platforms. Learn about the unique ecosystem and the lives of the fishing communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum for a deep dive into Khmer civilization, art, and history. The museum houses an impressive collection of statues, artifacts, and multimedia exhibits that provide excellent context for the temple visits.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Angkor Night Market, a curated market with local handicrafts, silk scarves, paintings, and street food. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at one of the many reputable spas nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the early boat departure.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — fresh fish dishes are the specialty. Budget around $8–12.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Market area — try num banh chok (Khmer noodles), grilled skewers, and fresh spring rolls. Budget $5–8 for a full street food spread.

day_by_day.notes: The boat tour to Tonlé Sap typically costs $15–25 per person depending on the village visited. November is an excellent time to visit as the lake is at its fullest after the monsoon season, making the floating village experience more dramatic.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by bus or private transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours by road, or 1 hour by domestic flight). If taking the bus, book a comfortable tourist bus like Giant Ibis for around $15. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into your mid-range accommodation. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of traditional Khmer architecture with gilded spires. The Silver Pagoda is named for its floor of 5,000 silver tiles and houses a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Riverside Promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. The area comes alive in the evening with locals, street vendors, and river breezes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop — local rice dishes or sandwiches available at rest stops.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) in Phnom Penh — a renowned social enterprise training street youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer tapas-style dishes. Budget $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance, especially during peak season. Giant Ibis is the most reliable and comfortable option. Alternatively, a domestic flight with Cambodia Angkor Air takes about 1 hour and costs $50–80 one way. The Royal Palace closes at midday (11:30 AM–2:30 PM) so plan the afternoon visit after 2:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison that is now a powerful and deeply moving memorial to the victims of the genocide. This is an essential and sobering part of understanding Cambodia's modern history. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) located about 15 km outside the city — an emotional but historically vital site with an excellent audio guide. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia, which houses the world's largest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Bassac Lane bar and restaurant alley for a more modern, cosmopolitan side of Phnom Penh. Enjoy craft cocktails and contemporary Cambodian fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near your hotel — try nom pang (Cambodian baguette sandwich) from a street stall for $1–2, a legacy of French colonial influence.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the National Museum — try kuy teav (Cambodian noodle soup) or a set lunch menu for $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — an upscale-casual Phnom Penh institution serving refined Khmer cuisine in a beautiful garden setting. Budget $15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — take breaks as needed and be respectful throughout. A combined tuk-tuk trip to both sites costs approximately $10–15. Hiring a knowledgeable local guide for these sites ($15–20) greatly enriches the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco landmark built in 1937 with a distinctive yellow dome. Browse stalls selling jewelry, clothing, electronics, and fresh produce. Then visit the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) for handicrafts, silk, and souvenirs at better prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic boat cruise on the Mekong River to visit Koh Dach (Silk Island) — a peaceful island where traditional silk weaving has been practiced for generations. Watch weavers at their looms and purchase authentic handmade silk scarves and textiles directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Phnom Penh by overnight bus or early evening flight to Sihanoukville (for the beach portion of the trip). Alternatively, take an afternoon bus to arrive by evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a French-style café near the riverside — Phnom Penh has excellent café culture. Try a café au lait and croissant for a colonial-era experience.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Koh Dach island at a riverside restaurant — fresh fish and Khmer dishes with scenic river views. Budget $6–10.
meals.dinner: Early dinner before departure at a riverside restaurant on Sisowath Quay — try Romdeng Restaurant for Cambodian cuisine with a social mission. Budget $12–18.

day_by_day.notes: The boat to Koh Dach departs from the ferry landing near the Japanese Friendship Bridge. Round trip costs approximately $5–8. Book your onward transport to Sihanoukville in advance — the journey takes 3–4 hours by bus ($10–15) or about 45 minutes by domestic flight ($50–70).

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Sihanoukville and transfer to Otres Beach — the calmer, more relaxed alternative to the busier main beaches. Check into a mid-range beachfront guesthouse. Spend the morning swimming in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters and relaxing on the pristine white sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip to the nearby islands — Koh Rong Samloem is highly recommended for its crystal-clear waters, vibrant coral reefs, and tranquil atmosphere. Enjoy snorkeling among colorful fish and coral, or simply relax on the stunning Saracen Bay beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Otres Beach for sunset. Watch the spectacular sunset over the Gulf of Thailand with a cold Angkor beer in hand. Enjoy a relaxed beachside dinner as the stars appear.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a beachside café — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Khmer iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Beach BBQ lunch on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled fresh seafood (prawns, squid, fish) on the beach. Budget $8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Otres Beach — fresh catch of the day, seafood curry, or grilled lobster. Budget $10–20 depending on selection.

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time for beach visits in Cambodia — the rainy season has just ended, leaving lush landscapes and calm seas. Boat trips to Koh Rong Samloem cost approximately $15–25 return. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystems. Sihanoukville's main town has become very developed — stick to Otres Beach for a more authentic, relaxed experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day island hopping tour visiting multiple islands around Sihanoukville — including Koh Rong, Bamboo Island (Koh Pos), and Snake Island (Koh Puos). Enjoy snorkeling, swimming, and exploring pristine beaches with minimal crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Otres Beach in the mid-afternoon. Rent a bicycle or motorbike and explore the local Otres Village — a charming community of local fishing families, small guesthouses, and laid-back beach bars. Visit a local fishing village to see traditional boat-building and daily fishing life.
day_by_day.evening: Final beach evening — enjoy a bonfire or bioluminescent plankton night swim (seasonal, but November can be excellent for this). Many boat operators offer guided night swims to see the magical glowing plankton around Koh Rong.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or tropical fruit breakfast at an Otres Beach café.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided on the island hopping boat tour, or eat at a beach shack on one of the islands.
meals.dinner: Farewell seafood feast at Holy Crab or a similar beachside restaurant on Otres Beach. Try the Kampot pepper crab — a Cambodian specialty. Budget $15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Island hopping tours can be booked through your hotel or local tour operators for approximately $20–35 per person including boat, snorkeling gear, and lunch. The bioluminescent plankton night swim is weather and season dependent — ask local operators about current conditions. Book through reputable operators for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the beach — enjoy a peaceful sunrise walk along Otres Beach, take a last swim, and soak in the tranquil Gulf of Thailand atmosphere. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from local beach vendors or the small market near Otres Village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Sihanoukville for Phnom Penh International Airport by bus or private transfer (3–4 hours). Alternatively, fly directly from Sihanoukville's regional airport if available. Arrive at Phnom Penh airport with time to spare for international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, rich Khmer culture, and beautiful tropical beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast at a beachside café — enjoy nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with fish sauce) or a fresh coconut with a view of the sea.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop in Sihanoukville town before departure — try a banh mi sandwich or Khmer noodle soup for a final taste of Cambodia.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 4–5 hours travel time from Otres Beach to Phnom Penh airport to ensure a comfortable connection. Keep some USD cash for departure taxes if not already included in your ticket. Cambodia does not charge a departure tax separately for most international flights, but confirm with your airline. Consider purchasing local honey, Kampot pepper, and handmade silk items as authentic Cambodian souvenirs before leaving.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within the Angkor Archaeological Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in and a welcome refreshment, take a leisurely orientation walk through the hotel gardens and surrounding temple grounds. Visit the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate for a first glimpse of the iconic stone faces — close enough for a relaxed first afternoon without overexertion after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel terrace or rooftop bar overlooking the jungle canopy. Enjoy a private welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring modern Khmer cuisine with locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel upon arrival — seasonal Cambodian salads, fresh spring rolls, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant — tasting menu featuring amok fish, lok lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice dessert paired with curated Cambodian wines

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out from your previous accommodation if needed. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to adjust to the time zone. November weather in Siem Reap is typically pleasant — dry season beginning with temperatures around 28–32°C.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience with a private expert guide. Arrive at Angkor Wat by 05:30 to secure a prime reflection pool viewing spot. After sunrise, embark on an exclusive guided tour of Angkor Wat's inner sanctuaries, bas-relief galleries depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central tower complex — areas often crowded later but serene in early morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the enigmatic Bayon Temple within Angkor Thom — marvel at 216 serene stone faces of Avalokiteshvara. Continue to Baphuon Temple and the Terrace of the Elephants. Enjoy a private picnic lunch arranged by the hotel in a shaded garden area near the Royal Palace ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive Apsara dance performance at a premium venue such as Koulen II Restaurant or a private hotel performance. Followed by dinner featuring royal Khmer cuisine in an atmospheric colonial setting.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast basket prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, Cambodian coffee, and pastries enjoyed near the Angkor Wat reflection pool
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic lunch near Angkor Thom — cold-pressed juices, charcuterie, Cambodian rice dishes, and tropical desserts
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer dinner at a premium Siem Reap restaurant such as Malis or Cuisine Wat Damnak — multi-course tasting menu with traditional Cambodian flavors elevated to fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Hire a licensed, expert English-speaking guide for the full day. Wear light, breathable clothing and comfortable walking shoes. Carry sunscreen, a hat, and a refillable water bottle. Temple dress code requires covered shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad Ta Prohm temple — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' — where ancient fig and silk-cotton trees dramatically embrace the stone ruins. Enjoy the mystical atmosphere with a private guide explaining the Jayavarman VII era history. Visit the nearby Banteay Kdei temple for a quieter, equally atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan temple, a vast monastic complex dedicated to Jayavarman VII's father, featuring stunning corridors and intricate carvings. Afterward, explore the peaceful Neak Pean — an artificial island temple set in a lotus-filled pond, accessible by a raised wooden walkway.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Pre Rup temple — one of the finest sunset viewpoints in the Angkor complex with panoramic views over the jungle. Return to Siem Reap town for a private tuk-tuk tour of the illuminated Old Market (Phsar Chas) district.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — eggs prepared to order, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), fresh tropical fruits, artisan breads, and premium Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a high-end riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — grilled Mekong fish, fresh herb salads, and coconut-based curries
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant or Mahob Restaurant — contemporary Cambodian cuisine in an elegant setting with curated cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm is best visited early morning or late afternoon to avoid tour groups. The afternoon light at Pre Rup is exceptional for photography. Bring a light jacket for the evening tuk-tuk ride.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — approximately 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily fine pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer art. A private air-conditioned vehicle and expert guide make the journey comfortable and enriching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (Cambodia Landmine Museum) nearby — a sobering and important cultural experience that provides deep insight into Cambodia's modern history and ongoing humanitarian efforts. Continue to Banteay Samré, a beautifully preserved Hindu temple rarely visited by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a private cooking class at a luxury villa or hotel — learn to prepare traditional Khmer dishes including fish amok, green mango salad, and palm sugar desserts with a master Cambodian chef.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before early departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local family-run premium restaurant near Banteay Srei — authentic Khmer home cooking featuring slow-cooked curries and fresh vegetables
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class in a beautifully set private dining experience at the villa or hotel

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (around 07:30) to reach Banteay Srei before the midday heat and tour groups. The road to Banteay Srei is well-paved. The cooking class should be booked in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the floating villages of Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Board a private luxury boat for a guided tour of Kompong Khleang, one of the more authentic and less-touristy floating villages, where entire communities live on stilted houses and floating platforms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour across the vast Tonlé Sap, observing local fishermen, floating schools, and the extraordinary ecosystem. Visit the Gecko Centre or similar environmental education center to learn about conservation efforts on the lake. Enjoy a private sunset cruise with champagne as the golden light reflects off the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and enjoy a leisurely evening at the hotel spa — indulge in a traditional Khmer massage using aromatic local herbs and oils, followed by a relaxing steam bath.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — buffet and à la carte options including Western and Cambodian selections
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the private boat — grilled lake fish, prawn dishes, and tropical fruit prepared by a private chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant or a reservation at Cuisine Wat Damnak — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake is at its highest water level in October–November, making the floating village experience more dramatic and accessible. Wear light clothing and bring sun protection on the boat. The spa should be reserved in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh — approximately 45 minutes of breathtaking aerial views over the Cambodian countryside, the Tonlé Sap, and the Mekong River. Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (such as Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and the famous Emerald Buddha. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia, housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and artifacts spanning 2,000 years.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Rosewood Sky Bar or Elephant Bar at Raffles with panoramic views over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence. Dinner in a colonial-era restaurant in the French Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel before helicopter departure — full spread including fresh pastries, eggs, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside fine-dining restaurant in Phnom Penh such as Malis Phnom Penh — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with river views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or Khéma La Poste — French-Cambodian fusion cuisine in an elegant colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter transfer well in advance through a reputable operator such as Helistar Cambodia. Confirm weight limits for luggage. The Royal Palace is closed on public holidays and Monday/Friday afternoons — verify timing with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential visit to Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a detention and torture center during the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). A private guide provides historical context and ensures a respectful, deeply informative experience. Follow with a visit to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) — an emotionally profound memorial site approximately 15 km from the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center for a visit to the vibrant Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) — browse premium silk scarves, handcrafted silver jewelry, lacquerware, and Cambodian gemstones. Enjoy a private shopping experience with a local artisan guide who can explain the cultural significance of each craft.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise on the Mekong River with champagne and canapés, watching the city's skyline transform in the golden hour. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Phnom Penh city lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full buffet with international and Cambodian options
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Russian Market — fresh sandwiches, Cambodian iced coffee, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sora Rooftop Bar & Restaurant at Rosewood Phnom Penh — elevated Cambodian and international cuisine with panoramic city views and curated cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted in most areas but always with respect. The Russian Market is best visited in the morning when it is cooler and less crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Phnom Penh to Kep — approximately 3 hours by private luxury vehicle through the Cambodian countryside. Stop en route at the ancient temple of Phnom Chisor — a hilltop Angkorian-era temple with sweeping views over the surrounding plains — and the Takeo Province salt flats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kep — a charming former French colonial beach resort town on the Gulf of Thailand. Check in to a luxury boutique property such as Knai Bang Chatt or The Veranda Natural Resort. Explore the famous Kep Crab Market — taste freshly caught blue swimmer crabs prepared with Kampot pepper, a world-renowned local specialty.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Kep beachfront promenade. Private beach dinner on the shore with lantern lighting — fresh seafood, Kampot pepper dishes, and chilled white wines under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure from Phnom Penh
meals.lunch: Fresh crab lunch at Kep Crab Market — steamed and pepper-fried blue crabs, grilled prawns, and coconut rice
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner at the resort — chef-curated seafood tasting menu featuring lobster, crab, and local fish with Kampot pepper and tropical fruit desserts

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time to visit Kep — the dry season brings calm seas and pleasant temperatures. Book the beach dinner experience in advance with the resort. The drive from Phnom Penh offers scenic countryside views — consider stopping at roadside stalls for fresh coconuts.

day_by_day.morning: Morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding in the calm waters of Kep Bay, arranged privately through the resort. Explore the small islands visible from shore — visit Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) by private boat for pristine white sand beaches, clear turquoise waters, and snorkeling among vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the mainland and visit Kep National Park — a forested hill behind the town with hiking trails through jungle to viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Thailand and the nearby islands. Visit the iconic ruined villas of Kep — haunting French colonial mansions abandoned since the Khmer Rouge era, slowly being reclaimed by the jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Day trip to nearby Kampot — a charming riverside colonial town approximately 25 km from Kep. Explore the old French Quarter, visit a Kampot pepper farm for a private tasting tour, and enjoy a sunset river cruise on the Praek Tuek Chhu River.

meals.breakfast: Tropical breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit platters, açaí bowls, eggs Benedict, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Beach barbecue lunch on Rabbit Island — freshly grilled fish, coconut rice, and tropical fruit served on the beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi in Kampot or the Rusty Keyhole — riverside fine dining with Cambodian-French fusion cuisine and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited on a clear day — November weather is generally ideal. Bring snorkeling gear (the resort can arrange rentals). The Kampot pepper farm visit should be arranged in advance — several farms offer premium private tours.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort, take one last swim in the sea or pool, and indulge in a farewell spa treatment — a traditional Cambodian herbal compress massage or a rejuvenating body wrap using local ingredients such as turmeric and lemongrass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle transfer back to Phnom Penh International Airport (approximately 3 hours) for your departure flight. En route, stop at a premium silk weaving cooperative or artisan workshop to purchase final souvenirs — hand-woven Cambodian silk scarves, silver jewelry, or Kampot pepper gift sets.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. If the flight departs late, enjoy a final dinner at the airport's premium lounge or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread with champagne mimosas, tropical fruits, eggs, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a roadside premium café en route to Phnom Penh or at the airport lounge
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or a final dinner near the airport — Cambodian classics such as lok lak, amok, and fresh spring rolls

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours for the drive to Phnom Penh Airport to account for traffic. Request the hotel to arrange a packed farewell gift — Kampot pepper, local coffee, or artisan crafts make wonderful mementos. Confirm all flight details and ensure luggage weight is within airline limits, especially with purchased souvenirs.
